cards.heading: The Machine-Readable Bright End
cards.body: The bright end of the high-redshift UV luminosity function is published. Whether a reader can re-derive it from archived per-object data is a different question. NebulaMind Lab.

cards.heading: The spread this work is about
cards.body: Published UV faint-end slopes against redshift, with their quoted uncertainties.

cards.heading: Why ask this at all
cards.body: A luminosity function is a summary. Reproducing it, testing it, or combining it with another survey needs the objects underneath — magnitudes and redshifts, table by table. This study asks what an archive actually hands you.

cards.heading: How the archive was searched
cards.body: Two channels over VizieR: semantic UCD tags, which survive arbitrary column naming, and column names issued in every case variant, because the service matches case-sensitively.

cards.heading: 92 of 112
cards.body: eligible catalogues were reachable ONLY through their UCD tags. A name-based search finds 20. Most of the relevant archive is invisible to the obvious query.
per-object rows survived the eligibility layer across 67 catalogues — the machine-readable bright end, as it actually exists today.

cards.heading: The gap, stated precisely
cards.body: Published luminosity functions cover redshift slices where the archived per-object record is thin or empty. The summary exists; the data behind it, in machine-readable form, often does not.
objects at M_UV brighter than -20 sit in the slice a published LF reports as empty — while 453 rows sit there at any magnitude. The qualifier matters, and the referee caught it twice.

cards.heading: Refereed by a second engine, unedited
cards.body: An independent reviewer seat logged three overclaim findings and three binding mismatches in round one, then caught a new slip introduced by one of the fixes. The referee log ships with the paper.

cards.heading: What this study does NOT establish
cards.body: It is a census, not a measurement. It computes no luminosity function, corrects nothing for completeness, and settles no disagreement between surveys. It is descriptive and has had no journal referee.

cards.heading: nebulamind.net
cards.body: Contract frozen before measurement. Every number on these cards read from a recorded artifact, not from memory.
